description: A normal standup: four categories exercised, four cards created, one duplicate skipped, and a post-write audit that confirms the board matches the plan.
note:
This scenario used to assert a category-dispute hold — Pass 2b's blind read disagreeing with Pass 2a across the new-versus-existing boundary. That expectation was removed after three consecutive re-recordings produced three different answers on the same fixture: held, then not, then not. The disagreement is a model judgement, and a cassette can pin what deterministic code does with a reply, never which reply arrives. Every gate, including the category dispute, is proven deterministically instead — 53 cases in contractGates.test.ts and an end-to-end hold in run.test.ts, all with scripted replies. Treating a lucky recording as a guarantee is how a fixture reads as stable for months and then fails for whoever re-records next, at the exact moment it is hardest to tell from a real regression.

Re-derived 2026-08-12, when the 2a/2b prompts were split into a cacheable system half and a per-item user half. Two things moved and neither was caused by that split. First, Pass 1 sometimes extracted a seventh item from the bare status line "Main flow is drafted"; that line was reworded to subordinate it to the actual commitment, which is the same fix scenario 02 got for the same reason — a fixture should be over-determined by its input. Second, item 5 (the flaky-auth-test investigation) now categorizes as SUBTASK of the nightly-build card rather than UPDATE on it, and 2a and 2b genuinely disagree about it: 2b's blind read still says UPDATE, and the dispute gate logs it and trusts 2a because both verdicts sit on the same side of the new-versus-existing boundary. That is the gate working, not failing. The evidence that the system/user split is behaviourally neutral is direct rather than assumed: Pass 1's prompt fingerprint is byte-identical across the change (ced7582a8aee both sides) while its reply differed, and a paired A/B of the same 2a prompt sent split versus joined returned the same verdict on three consecutive runs.
